name: refuse-file-write-grant
text:
Refuse a write grant that names a file.

A grant is a directory prefix. `grants.rs` says so in its first paragraph
and `RootWriter` requires it: every write root is opened with
`Dir::open_ambient_dir`.

A lead dividing work across a team narrows each worker to the unit it was
given, and a unit is usually one file. That narrowing is accepted, recorded
as the child's `effective_write`, and then cannot be opened. The worker dies
at construction with

    grants.write: Not a directory (os error 20)

which names neither the worker nor the call that made it. Its episode log is
created and left empty, the lead reads only "exited without episode/end",
and it goes on to do the work itself. The run reports `completed` with a
units list naming workers that never ran, so nothing about the outcome says
the team did not function.

The empty write narrowing a few lines above is refused for exactly this
reason, and the comment there states the principle: the child "would die at
construction with nothing said about the call that caused it, so the call is
what is refused". A file-shaped root is the same failure. Refuse it too, and
name the directory to grant, so the lead can act on the message.

checks/run.sh runs the checks this task is judged on: the tests of foe-core, clippy with warnings denied on the same crates, and scripts/loc.sh.

Follow AGENTS.md. Run the checks it names. When you finish, or when you cannot, report your outcome.
